_comment: EACH STDIO SERVER RUNS DIRECTLY WHERE ITS BINARY EXISTS, AND WAITS FOR THE
BOOTSTRAP WHERE IT DOES NOT. A workstation that has the binary execs it at
once and is unchanged; a remote session starts before
.github/scripts/cloud-bootstrap.sh has finished installing serena, so there
the wrapper waits up to 180 seconds and then execs.
NEVER `exit 0` ON A WORKSTATION. The obvious wrapper — exit 0 unless the
remote marker is set — makes every stdio server remote-only, which would
silently disable the two that work here today. A workstation missing the
binary exits NON-ZERO and fails to connect, exactly as it does without any
wrapper: a server that is meant to be there and is not must say so.
`sonarqube` is http, not stdio: nothing is installed for it, and remotely
the credential proxy attaches the token for its host.
`sonarqube`'s headers are the WORKSTATION's, and they are deliberately
unconditional for now. Remotely the credential proxy attaches the token for
that host, and whether it OVERRIDES a header the client sends or requires it
absent is not yet measured — design D6 records it as the question the first
remote session settles. Guessing a `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` conditional here
would encode an answer nobody has; if the proxy needs the header absent, the
fix is one line and it lands with the measurement.

args: command -v uvx >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec uvx mcp-server-docker; [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE" = "1" ] || [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE" = "true" ] || exit 1; for _ in $(seq 180); do command -v uvx >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec uvx mcp-server-docker; sleep 1; done; exit 1

command -v serena >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec serena start-mcp-server --context claude-code --project-from-cwd; [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE" = "1" ] || [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE" = "true" ] || exit 1; for _ in $(seq 180); do command -v serena >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec serena start-mcp-server --context claude-code --project-from-cwd; sleep 1; done; exit 1
